# Fixtures

| Directory | Contents |
|---|---|
| `sample/` | a small project written for the tests |
| `figures/` | a small project with an SVG, a PDF and a JPEG figure, for the goldens of the PDF and the EPUB (`OutputGoldenSpec`); the test copies its fonts in as `fonts/ja.otf` and `fonts/latin.otf` |
| `tempest/` | *The Tempest* by William Shakespeare, set horizontally |
| `kanikosen/` | 『蟹工船』小林多喜二, set vertically |
| `pd/` | ten public-domain books that are hard to set ([docs/adr/0026](../../../../docs/adr/0026-ten-public-domain-fixtures.md)) |

`tempest/tempest.gm`, `kanikosen/kanikosen.gm` and the `.gm` of every book
of `pd/` are generated by `scripts/fixtures/fetch-public-domain.sh`, which
downloads the texts, checks their SHA-256, converts them with
`golem-fixtures` (the converters in `modules/golem-fixtures`, run through
`cabal run`;
[docs/adr/0023](../../../../docs/adr/0023-fixture-converters-without-python.md),
[docs/adr/0026](../../../../docs/adr/0026-ten-public-domain-fixtures.md)) and
formats them with `golem fmt`.
Do not edit them by hand. To make them again:

```sh
GOLEM=$(cabal list-bin golem) scripts/fixtures/fetch-public-domain.sh
```

The source texts are not committed.

## Sources

- *The Tempest*: Project Gutenberg eBook #23042, the Cambridge edition
  (1863) edited by W. G. Clark and W. A. Wright. The play is in the public
  domain. The converter drops the Project Gutenberg header and licence,
  the transcriber's note, the footnotes and the textual notes; the result
  carries no Project Gutenberg trademark. Verse is set with `@style verse`. The
  source marks verse only by its line breaks, so the converter guesses it
  and takes a few short prose speeches whose lines all start with capitals
  for verse (two in Act I, Scene I).
- 『蟹工船』: 青空文庫 図書カード No.1465（底本「蟹工船・党生活者」新潮文庫）。
  著作権の保護期間は満了している。入力者、校正者と底本の情報は、青空文庫の
  ファイルにあるとおり `kanikosen.gm` の末尾に残している。

## The ten books of `pd/`

Each book is a Golem project like the two above: the English books are set
horizontally on A5 in Source Serif, the Japanese books vertically on B6 in
Noto Serif JP, with the page grids of *The Tempest* and 『蟹工船』.
All ten are in the public domain in Japan and in the United States: every
author and translator died before 1968 (the Japanese term of fifty years
after death, extended for the nationals of the Allied Powers, ran out
before the term became seventy years on 2018-12-30), and every work was
published before 1931. The Project Gutenberg header and licence are
dropped (the result carries no Project Gutenberg trademark); the Aozora
Bunko colophon, with its typists, proofreaders and base edition, is kept
at the end of each Japanese book.

### What the converters do not carry over

- `merry-wives`: `gutenberg-play` is the converter of *The Tempest*, unchanged
  (docs/adr/0023). In the list of characters, the braces that group two
  or three names are kept as `}` without their columns, and the
  footnote of the list and the title (`THE` / `MERRY WIVES OF WINDSOR.`)
  become items of the list.
- `frogs`: the source wraps some long lines of verse in the middle; a line
  is joined to the one before only when that one is 66 characters or
  longer and the line starts in lowercase, so some wraps remain.
  Stage directions in italic that span several blocks are italic only in
  the first.
- `snark`: the centred title lines are not centred (a paragraph style has no
  alignment); the contents list is kept as lines of verse.
- `elements-of-style`: the two columns become a table with an empty header
  row. The contents list loses its page-number column (each entry becomes a
  quotation ending with the page number). The word list of "Words often
  misspelled" (one word per line) becomes one paragraph.
- `nightmare-abbey`: Greek is transliterated in the source
  (`[Greek: philoschios]`) and stays so. The names of the speakers of the
  dialogues are paragraphs of their own, as in the source.
  No passage is marked as French or Latin, so they are hyphenated with
  the English patterns.
- Aozora Bunko (all five): gaiji given only by a JIS X 0213 plane-row-cell
  number, without a Unicode code point, become `〓` (6 in 高野聖, 7 in 一握の
  砂, 2 in 春と修羅, 14 in 平将門). 傍線, 地付き and 地からの字上げ,
  行右小書き, 段階の小さな文字 and ページの左右中央 are dropped and the text
  kept. Kaeriten and the okurigana of kunten are small characters in the
  line (`[style kunten: …]`), not at the lower left of the kanji. 同行見出し
  become bold.

## Fonts

Each book of the two above carries its fonts under `fonts/`, with their
licences, so the fixture builds as it is (`golem build` in its directory).

- `kanikosen/fonts/NotoSerifJP-Regular.otf`: Noto Serif CJK JP 2.003, the
  Japanese subset OTF from https://github.com/notofonts/noto-cjk (release
  `Serif2.003`, `12_NotoSerifJP.zip`), SHA-256
  `2c9a12dbd4f2408c4610c7ee84a108b62d7236c3775baed618c64d9cb44b2f04`.
  SIL Open Font License 1.1.
- `tempest/fonts/SourceSerifVariable-Roman.ttf`: Source Serif, the test
  font of golem-font (variable; Golem uses its default instance).
  SIL Open Font License 1.1.

The ten books of `pd/` do not commit their fonts (`.gitignore`), to keep
34 MB of copies out of the repository. `scripts/fixtures/copy-fonts.sh`
copies the fonts and licences of `kanikosen/` into the Japanese books and
those of `tempest/` into the English ones; `fetch-public-domain.sh` runs it.

```sh
scripts/fixtures/copy-fonts.sh
cd modules/golem-driver/test/fixtures/pd/koya-hijiri && golem build
```

## Tests

The golem-driver tests check each book of `pd/` without errors (as
`golem check` does). With `GOLEM_PD_BOOKS` set, they build every target of
each book, check the PDF with qpdf and its writing mode; this takes about
35 seconds for the ten.

```sh
GOLEM_PD_BOOKS=1 cabal test golem-driver --test-options='-p 0026'
```
